4500: adverb from a derivative of (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash:--with a great noise.

4503: of Hebrew origin (רוּת); Ruth, a Moabitess:--Ruth.
4504: of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian:--Rufus.
4505: prolongation from ῥύομαι in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded):--lane, street.

4509: of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity:--filth.

4512: from ῥύομαι; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face):--wrinkle.

4516: from the base of ῥώννυμι; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy:--Rome.

4527: of Hebrew origin (שֶׁלַח); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch :--Sala.

4530: probably from the same as σαλεύω; Salim, a place in Palestine:--Salim.

4550: from σήπω; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare πονηρός.
4551: feminine of σάπφειρος; Sapphire, an Israelitess:--Sapphira.
4552: of Hebrew origin (סַפִּיר); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:--sapphire.
4553: apparently of Hebrew origin (שָׂרַג); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work:--basket.
4554: plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor:--Sardis.
4555: from the same as σάρδιος; sardine (λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.

4576: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore:--devout, religious, worship.

4589: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁת); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch:--Seth.
4590: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁם); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:-- Sem.

4596: from (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric):--silk.

4598: from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; moth-eaten:--motheaten.
4599: from (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power):--strengthen.
